jobs.title: Director, Product Management
jobs.description:
Opentext - The Information Company

OpenText is a global leader in information management, where innovation, creativity, and collaboration are the key components of our corporate culture. As a member of our team, you will have the opportunity to partner with the most highly regarded companies in the world, tackle complex issues, and contribute to projects that shape the future of digital transformation.

AI-First. Future-Driven. Human-Centered.

At OpenText, AI is at the heart of everything we do—powering innovation, transforming work, and empowering digital knowledge workers. We are hiring talent AI can't replace to help us shape the future of information management. Join us.

Director, Product Management
- Business Network Solutions - Full Time on Site Richmond Hill / Waterloo, ON

The Opportunity

We are seeking a Director, Product Management to lead the strategy, roadmap, and lifecycle management of our Business Network Solutions portfolio, including B2B Messaging, Managed File Transfer (MFT), Message Transport, Electronic Data Interchange (EDI), Communications, and related connectivity services.

Your Impact

This role is responsible for identifying market opportunities, defining product and service strategies, managing product roadmaps, and partnering closely with Sales, Marketing, Operations, Engineering, and key customers to drive growth and customer success. The ideal candidate combines strong product management expertise with a deep understanding of B2B communications, trading partner connectivity, message exchange platforms, managed file transfer, supply chain integration, and cloud-based business services.

What The Role Offers

Define and execute the product strategy and roadmap for Business Network Solutions, ensuring alignment with business objectives and market needs.
Manage the full product lifecycle, from market assessment and business case development to launch, enhancement, migration and retirement.
Engage customers, partners, analysts and internal stakeholders to identify market opportunities and translate customer, industry and regulatory needs into product initiatives.
Leverage AI to improve product management effectiveness, accelerate decision-making and enhance the product development lifecycle.
Drive the evolution of B2B Messaging, Message Transport, Communications, MFT, EDI and related network services.
Conduct competitive analysis, market assessments and pricing reviews to identify growth, differentiation and profitability opportunities.
Partner with Sales, Marketing, Operations, Engineering and Managed Services to drive go-to-market strategies, product positioning and successful launches.
Monitor portfolio performance, customer satisfaction, adoption and revenue; present roadmaps and strategic recommendations while supporting investment, build/buy/partner and portfolio decisions.

What You Need To Succeed

Bachelor's degree in Business, IT, Computer Science or related field; MBA preferred.
7+ years of product management or product strategy experience in enterprise technology, B2B integration, communications or network services.
Experience with B2B Messaging, EDI, MFT, Message Transport, Supply Chain Integration, Enterprise SaaS or Managed Services.
Strong understanding of product management practices, software development lifecycle, roadmaps, business cases, pricing and go-to-market strategies.
Excellent communication, presentation and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to influence cross-functional teams in global, matrixed organizations.

Preferred Skills

Deep knowledge of B2B messaging, EDI, MFT, communications networks, API connectivity and digital supply chains, with the ability to translate technical capabilities into business value.
Strong analytical and financial skills, including market assessment, revenue opportunities and portfolio performance.
Proven ability to balance strategic planning with execution, manage competing priorities and drive results in a fast-paced environment.

One Last Thing

OpenText is more than just a corporation, it's a global community where trust is foundational, the bar is raised, and outcomes are owned.

Join us on our mission to drive positive change through privacy, technology, and collaboration. At OpenText, we don't just have a culture; we have character. Choose us because you want to be part of a company that embraces innovation and empowers its employees to make a difference.

OpenText's commitment to diversity and inclusion surpasses legal requirements, evident in our Equal Employment Opportunity Statement of Policy which promotes a respectful and empowering environment for employees of all backgrounds, culture, national origin, race, color, gender, gender identification, sexual orientation, family status, age, veteran status, disability, religion, or other basis protected by applicable laws.

If you need assistance and/or a reasonable accommodation due to a disability during the application or recruiting process, please submit a ticket at Ask HR. Our proactive approach fosters collaboration, innovation, and personal growth, enriching OpenText's vibrant workplace.

Compensation:
At OpenText, we offer a thoughtfully designed benefits package that supports your physical, emotional, and financial wellbeing. As you move through the hiring process, we’re happy to provide more details about our compensation programs, including variable and commission compensation opportunities for eligible roles, vacation entitlement, and paid time off.

AI Usage Disclosure:
As part of our commitment to transparency, we use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to assist in various stages of our recruitment process, including resume screening, candidate matching, interview scheduling, and communications. These tools are designed to improve efficiency, reduce bias, and enhance candidate experience. All decisions regarding hiring are made by qualified human professionals, and we continuously monitor our AI systems to ensure fairness and compliance with applicable regulations.

jobs.title: Senior Director, Finance (Non-Profit Housing)
jobs.description:
About Matrix360

Matrix360 is a social impact business helping to build the commercial real estate and development (CRED) industry – an industry responsible for creating and building our cities and communities.

For more than two decades, Matrix360 has been at the forefront of building great and successful teams. We're not your average talent management company—we are trailblazers committed to building diverse and inclusive workplaces. We partner with organizations that pave the way for business growth and success.

We believe in the uniqueness of every team and organization. Understanding and centering care in everything we do is our priority. We take a human-centered approach, connecting talent with opportunities, advising leaders on equitable policies, and transforming workplace cultures for the better. At Matrix360, we are the champions of diversity and equity in the CRED industry.

We firmly believe in providing equal access and opportunities to all individuals, ensuring accommodation and inclusion in every aspect of employment, services, programs, and activities.

If you require accommodation or this information in an alternative format at any stage of the search process, contact us at info@matrix360.ca or 416 703 3400.

About Our Client

Raising the Roof (RTR) is a nationally registered charity with the primary goal of delivering long term solutions to homelessness in Canada. Previously to 2020 the organization was known for their toque campaign as well as contributions to homelessness awareness and research. In response to the magnitude of today’s homelessness crisis, RTR has pivoted to focus primarily on homelessness prevention through the development and operation of affordable rental housing. Their portfolio has grown significantly since this work began in 2020 with 70 units in operation by the end of 2024 and over 400 units currently under development.

Most of the units in operation are located in the GTA. Other communities within which RTR has active development sites or operating units include Orillia, Barrie, Sudbury, Winnipeg and St. John’s. The goal is to one day develop and operate housing across all provinces and territories in Canada.

They operate a mix of market and affordable units across a range of different profiles with corresponding tenant acuity, affordability and levels of support. In each community we serve, RTR forms a partnership with at least one housing provider partner – typically a non-profit group that will refer tenants, provide support services and (sometimes) provide property management services. RTR has some head lease arrangement but predominantly holds leases directly with tenants and hires contractors accordingly to manage the needs of the tenants and real estate operations.

For more information about our client, please connect with us.

Senior Director, Finance

On behalf of our Client, a growing not-for-profit housing platform and national charity, we are seeking a Senior Director, Finance to provide strategic financial leadership and operational oversight for the organization as they expand their national affordable housing development and operating portfolio.

In this newly created role, you would build out and lead the finance function while working closely with the Director of Housing Development & Operations, and the Director of Strategic Initiatives & Partnerships to support the planning, financing, and delivery of housing projects across Canada.

The successful candidate will be a highly motivated team player, with the ability to work in a dynamic and fast-paced environment. They will be able to work collaboratively with multiple internal/external teams. The ideal candidate will be someone who enjoys putting structure in place while staying hands-on and close to the day-to-day.

Base salary for this position is $120k - $150k based on level of industry experience and exposure, plus a fully remote working style, comprehensive benefits and vacation. Our client is an advocate for equity and diversity and recognizes the importance of leadership engagement within its framework.

Responsibilities

1. Strategic Financial Leadership

Serve as a key strategic advisor to the Executive Director and Board of Directors on financial sustainability, capital strategy, and organizational growth.
Develop long-term financial strategies aligned with the company's mission to prevent homelessness through housing development.
Support multi-year financial modelling for the organization’s housing pipeline and operating portfolio.
Provide financial leadership support in evaluating new development opportunities, acquisitions, and strategic partnerships.

2. Housing Development Finance and Capital Structuring

Work with the Director of Housing Development & Operations to ensure financial feasibility and sustainability of development projects.
Supports the structuring of affordable housing development projects across multiple provinces.
Supports the creation of development pro-formas, project budgets, and operating projections.
Supports the structuring and management of complex capital stacks, including:

3. Housing Portfolio Financial Management and Operations

Leads financial management of the organization’s housing asset portfolio, including operating budgets, reserves, and long-term financial sustainability.
Oversees portfolio-level financial reporting and performance metrics.
Ensure appropriate financial planning for capital repairs, lifecycle costs, and reserve funds.
Work closely with the Director of Housing Development & Operations to ensure effective financial transition from development to operations.
Leads in the areas of managing project risk, finalizing construction budgets, contingency management, and development partner oversight.

4. Social Finance and Innovative Capital

Lead strategies for utilizing social finance tools to support housing development and portfolio growth.
Work collaboratively with the senior leadership to identify new capital partnerships, explore innovative financing mechanisms, develop opportunities for impact investment.
Oversee the development of financing structures such as community or social bonds, impact investment vehicles, loan guarantees and credit enhancement, program-related investments from foundations.

5. Financial Management and Organizational Operations

Oversee all financial operations including accounting, reporting, budgeting, investment strategy, and cash flow management.
Lead annual budgeting and multi-year financial planning processes.
Leads in the areas of treasury management, construction draw management, debt covenant monitoring, interest rate risk management.
Ensure accurate financial reporting across programs, housing developments, and partnerships.
Strengthen financial systems to support a growing national housing developer.

6. Human Resources Policy Compliance and Organizational Administration

Ensure compliance with employment legislation, workplace regulations, and organizational HR policies.
Oversee implementation and monitoring of HR policies including compensation frameworks, benefits administration, and workplace practices.
Support the Executive Director and leadership team in maintaining strong HR governance and organizational risk management.
Work with senior leadership to support workforce planning as the housing development pipeline and portfolio expand.

7. Governance, Compliance and Risk Management

Ensure compliance with charitable regulations, funding agreements, lender requirements, and financial reporting standards.
Lead annual audits and relationships with external auditors.
Maintain strong internal controls and financial governance practices.
Support the Board Finance and Audit Committee with clear financial reporting and risk oversight.
Contribute to enterprise risk management related to development, operations, finance, and HR.

8. Collaborative Leadership

Guide the strategic growth of Raising the Roof’s housing development portfolio.
Align financial, operational, and partnership strategies to support project delivery.
Coordinate capital planning, development pipelines, and partnership development.
Support organizational growth while balancing impact, financial sustainability, and risk management.

Qualifications

CPA designation required (CPA, CA, CMA, or CGA)
5+ years of progressive financial leadership experience.
Strong knowledge of ASPE accounting and charitable reporting standards
Senior financial leadership experience in affordable housing, real estate development, non-profit housing, or social infrastructure sectors considered an asset.
Demonstrated experience structuring financing for housing or real estate development projects.
Experience managing housing operations or real estate portfolios.
Experience working with social finance instruments and blended capital models.

By providing us with a copy of your resume and any subsequent personal information directly, you understand that it has been furnished with your consent for the purpose of possible disclosure to our client, who has agreed to comply with our Privacy Policy and Confidentiality Policy. We will only disclose your personal information to clients with your prior knowledge and consent.

Matrix360 believes in and continuously operates from the highest search and talent management ethics level. We continue to respect the privacy and confidentiality of the personal information provided to us. We are committed to guarding your information securely and managing it per our legal responsibilities wherever we operate, including the Personal Information Protection and Electronic Documents Act ("PIPEDA") in Canada.

For more information on our Privacy and Confidentiality Policies please contact us at: info@matrix360.ca or 416.703.3400.

Follow Us
LinkedIn: https://go.matrix360.ca/LinkedIn
Instagram: @matrix360_inc

Our Purpose

At Deloitte, our Purpose is to make an impact that matters. We exist to inspire and help our people, organizations, communities, and countries to thrive by building a better future. Our work underpins a prosperous society where people can find meaning and opportunity. It builds consumer and business confidence, empowers organizations to find imaginative ways of deploying capital, enables fair, trusted, and functioning social and economic institutions, and allows our friends, families, and communities to enjoy the quality of life that comes with a sustainable future. And as the largest 100% Canadian-owned and operated professional services firm in our country, we are proud to work alongside our clients to make a positive impact for all Canadians.

By living our Purpose, we will make an impact that matters.

Have many careers in one Firm.
Enjoy flexible, proactive, and practical benefits that foster a culture of well-being and connectedness.
Learn from deep subject matter experts through mentoring and on the job coaching

--

What will your typical day look like?

This leadership opportunity is suited to an established communications professional with significant experience in executive and internal communications, employee engagement, organizational transformation, crisis communications, and issues management. The successful candidate will bring strong executive presence, a deep understanding of business strategy, and experience advising a CEO and translating leadership priorities into clear, compelling communications that drive understanding, engagement, and action.

Working closely with the Chief Executive Officer and national leadership, this individual will develop and execute the executive communications strategy for Deloitte Canada and Chile, lead a high-performing internal communications team, and support the firm’s purpose, values, culture, and reputation.

About The Team

Deloitte Canada and Chile is seeking a senior internal communications professional to support our Chief Executive Officer. This role will be the strategic partner and advisor to the CEO to create understanding, inspiration, engagement and action with our partners and people. By leading a team for both strategy development and implementation, this role will continually enhance our purpose, values, and culture by communicating leadership’s vision and business strategy.

Enough About Us, Let’s Talk About You

Key responsibilities:

Blend the art and science of communications to produce clarity of action for our partners and people
Lead the development of the executive communications strategy, including objectives, priorities, messaging, and implementation plans to achieve business results
Develop specific communication strategies that support growth, acquisitions, transformation, and expansion into new markets
Enhance existing capabilities to continuously understand and adapt to the communications needs of our internal audience
Lead, mentor, and develop a high-performing internal communications team
Be a leader on our issues management team to enhance and protect the reputation of the firm

Qualifications and characteristics:

More than 15 years of experience in progressively senior internal communications roles within large matrixed organizations, including at least one role directly supporting a CEO
An extraordinarily strong executive presence and ability to build immediate confidence with leaders
A record of measurable success and new thinking to create action-based results
A deep understanding of business dynamics and strategy to supplement communications experience
Strong experience in crisis communications and issues management
Proven ability to develop and support staff to enhance their progression

Total Rewards

The salary range for this position is $140,000 - $260,000, and individuals may be eligible to participate in our bonus program. Deloitte is fair and competitive when it comes to the salaries of our people. We regularly benchmark across a variety of positions, industries, sectors, targets, and levels. Our approach is grounded on recognizing people's unique strengths and contributions and rewarding the value that they deliver.

Our Total Rewards Package extends well beyond traditional compensation and benefit programs and is designed to recognize employee contributions, encourage personal wellness, and support firm growth. Along with a competitive base salary and variable pay opportunities, we offer a wide array of initiatives that differentiate us as a people-first organization. On top of our regular paid vacation days, some examples include: $4,000 per year for mental health support benefits, a $1,300 flexible benefit spending account, firm-wide closures known as "Deloitte Days", dedicated days of for learning (known as Development and Innovation Days), flexible work arrangements and a hybrid work structure.

Our promise to our people: Deloitte is where potential comes to life.

Be yourself, and more.

We are a group of talented people who want to learn, gain experience, and develop skills. Wherever you are in your career, we want you to advance.

You Shape How We Make Impact.

Diverse perspectives and life experiences make us better. Whoever you are and wherever you’re from, we want you to feel like you belong here. We provide flexible working options to support you and how you can contribute.

Be the leader you want to be

Some guide teams, some change culture, some build essential expertise. We offer opportunities and experiences that support your continuing growth as a leader.

Have as many careers as you want.

We are uniquely able to offer you new challenges and roles – and prepare you for them. We bring together people with unique experiences and talents, and we are the place to develop a lasting network of friends, peers, and mentors.

The next step is yours

At Deloitte, we are all about doing business inclusively – that starts with having diverse colleagues of all abilities. Deloitte encourages applications from all qualified candidates who represent the full diversity of communities across Canada. This includes, but is not limited to, people with disabilities, candidates from Indigenous communities, and candidates from the Black community in support of living our values, creating a culture of Diversity Equity and Inclusion and our commitment to our AccessAbility Action Plan, Reconciliation Action Plan and the BlackNorth Initiative.

We encourage you to connect with us at accessiblecareers@deloitte.ca if you require an accommodation for the recruitment process (including alternate formats of materials, accessible meeting rooms or other accommodations) or indigenouscareers@deloitte.ca for any questions relating to careers for Indigenous peoples at Deloitte (First Nations, Inuit, Métis).

When you apply, we will review your application using Deloitte's Global Talent Standards to ensure a consistent recruitment experience. Our recruitment advisors and hiring teams will utilize human screening combined with AI technology to help identify the skills and qualities that matter most to our business, while safeguarding your privacy and using AI responsibly.

Deloitte Canada has 20 offices with representation across most of the country. We acknowledge that Deloitte offices stand on traditional, treaty, and unceded territories in what is now known as Canada. We recognize that Indigenous Peoples have been the caretakers of this land since time immemorial, nurturing its resources and preserving its natural beauty. We acknowledge this land is still home to many First Nations, Inuit, and Métis Peoples, who continue to maintain their deep connection to the land and its sacred teachings. jobs.title: Director of IT
jobs.description:
Guru Studio is a creative-driven entertainment company and an industry leader in animated storytelling. For over twenty years, our studio has brought to life some of the most recognizable and beloved children’s properties in the world.

We’re always looking for passionate and committed talent, so come join our dynamic and growing team!

Guru is proud to offer our team members meaningful learning and developmental opportunities! You will work alongside a wide range of talent in a positive and supportive environment where we want to see success in each individual.

We're looking for a talented and experienced Director of IT - come join our team!

The Director of IT will supervise and manage the IT department’s daily and long-term operations to allow for growth in a fast paced and rapidly expanding internationally renowned animation studio. This role is a management position for a very sophisticated tech-based company and requires clear and effective leadership and visionary thinking. This role reports to the VP of Technology.

Duties and Responsibilities include but will not be limited to:

Management + Supervision

Manage a department of IT professionals in their day to day operational functions and all of their responsibilities including server, desktop, and communications infrastructure, ensuring a reasonable level of in-studio IT support is available during regular business hours.
Set goals and milestones for all IT staff. Review their performance and report to the VP of Technology.
Liaise with all heads of production and business operations to ensure IT department’s efforts are coordinated to meet everyone’s needs (get information on studio upcoming projects, determine production resources needs, communication and delivery requirements and issue and follow up on all appropriate tasks).

Facility Infrastructure Planning

Ensure all physical services (leased space, electrical, HVAC, floor load etc) at the studio and in the data centre are able to support IT equipment and services and that the equipment is compatible and fully integrated with physical services.
Manage all budget needs for the IT department: create, present and revise purchase orders, follow up on approvals, ensure purchasing documentation is digitized, recorded and stored in a central repository, maintain IT inventory lists.
Budget for, acquire and maintain appropriate licenses for all software needed for production and business operations.
Maintain studio growth plan with the President, the VP of Technology and VP of Finance and Business Affairs.
Gather and organize purchasing research with guidance from relevant IT personnel.
Prepare projected equipment cost information for studio project bidding purposes.
Implement, manage and supervise IT desktop ticketing systems.
Schedule IT all operations including: personnel, technical maintenance, internal meetings and finance and budget related deadlines.
Ensure regular maintenance and upgrades are done to all IT infrastructure to ensure a secure and well-functioning IT environment.
Work with studio stakeholders to implement any studio expansion or move.

Knowledgebase

Maintain IT documentation/wiki (oversee, coordinate and arrange information input and creation of diagrams, organize the structure of documentation/wiki, propose new sections).
Create and Maintain IT procedures and policies (coordinate with the input from the VP of Technology).
Guru methodology asks for employees who will go above and beyond; in staying informed on upcoming technologies, most cost-effective vendors and taking the initiative in implementing forward thinking planning within each department.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field (or equivalent practical experience).
5+ years of progressive experience in IT infrastructure and operations, including 1–2+ years in a senior management or director-level role.
Previous experience working in an animation, VFX, gaming, or post-production environment is considered a strong asset.
Deep expertise in enterprise server architecture, high-speed networking, SAN/NAS storage, render farms, cloud/hybrid workflows, and multi-OS environments (Linux, Windows, macOS).
Strong familiarity with 2D/3D creative software pipelines (e.g., Maya, Houdini, Nuke, Harmony, Adobe Creative Cloud) and managing enterprise software licensing.
Hands-on experience overseeing physical data center requirements (electrical, HVAC, floor load) and leading studio office expansions or relocations.
Proven track record managing IT helpdesk ticketing systems, asset inventories, preventative maintenance schedules, and studio security/IP protection standards (such as TPN compliance).
Extensive experience negotiating vendor contracts, managing purchase orders, and forecasting equipment costs for project bidding.
Strong organizational skills with experience building and maintaining structured IT wikis, network diagrams, SOPs, and company-wide IT policies.

Why Join Guru?

We create a collaborative and creatively fulfilling work environment by promoting courage, purpose, inspiration, integrity, transparency, and empowerment as our core values
We take great pride in our work and we always ensure it reflects a high standard of quality and creativity
We encourage individuals to grow with us by offering learning opportunities that encourage skill development and growth
We are proud to support philanthropic initiatives that support our local and global community through our charity committee Guru Gives
We offer health and wellness support through an extensive benefits plan and extended mental health services and initiatives

Guru is committed to providing an inclusive work environment that celebrates the diversity of its employees. We are dedicated to employment equity and welcome applications from people from all Indigenous groups, races, religions, genders and people with disabilities.

We are committed to providing an accessible candidate experience during our recruitment process and are committed to fostering an inclusive and accessible ‎environment where candidates and ‎employees feel valued and respected. Guru strives to respect the dignity and ‎‎independence of people with disabilities and is committed to giving them the same ‎‎opportunity to succeed in the recruitment process as all other candidates. If you have a disability, you may request ‎to be accommodated at any time. Guru will work with all candidates to ‎‎accommodate individual accessibility needs to the point of undue hardship.

Guru Studio would like to thank all applicants for your interest, however only those who qualify for an interview will be contacted.

Accommodations are available on request for candidates taking part in all aspects of the selection process. Guru Studio is an equal opportunity employer.

Please note this is an In-Studio Work position

jobs.title: Senior Director, Strategic Accounts & Business Development
jobs.description:
Crofters is growing and we are seeking an energetic, reliable & flexible team player to join our Team. Here’s your chance to join a highly skilled team of professionals at one of North America’s pioneering brands in the organic food movement! Crofters Food Ltd, known in the grocery aisles as Crofters Organic Fruit Spreads, is the leading manufacturer of organic jams, jellies and fruit spreads in North America. Headquartered in picturesque Parry Sound, Ontario, about two hours north of Toronto, we manufacture a vast array of fruit-based spreads sold in stores across Canada, the United States, and select international markets. From the way we source our fruit, to the way we carefully manufacture our products using forward-thinking sustainable processing techniques, to our innovative, health-conscious formulations, every aspect of our operations receives the care and attention they deserve. A small but mighty team, join us as we look to aggressively scale our business on our mission to become one of the leading organic food brands in North America.

Position Summary

The Sr. Director of Strategic Accounts & New Business Development is responsible for growing Crofter’s largest US retail relationships and building the pipeline of new customers and channels that will drive the company’s next stage of growth. This role directly owns Walmart US, Kroger, Publix, HEB, Trader Joe’s and Harris Teeter, leads the e-commerce channel including Amazon, and supports the Costco business in partnership with the VP of Strategic Accounts, with the long-term goal of owning the Club channel.

Key Responsibilities

1. Strategic Account Leadership

Directly own the Walmart US, Kroger, Publix, HEB, Trader Joe’s and Harris Teeter relationships, including annual customer plans, joint business plans, line reviews and annual negotiations.
Build and execute customer plans that deliver sales, distribution and profit targets for each account within the approved trade budget.
Manage trade spend, the promotional calendar and pricing execution for assigned accounts, with a clear focus on trade ROI.
Develop senior-level relationships with buyers, category managers and customer leadership teams.
Use retailer POS, portal and syndicated data to identify growth opportunities and lead fact-based business reviews.

2. E-Commerce

Own the e-commerce channel, including Amazon, with accountability for sales, profitability and channel strategy.
Manage the Amazon relationship, including vendor or seller operations, assortment, pricing, promotions and advertising investment.
Drive digital shelf execution across Amazon and retailer .com sites: content, ratings and reviews, search visibility and in-stock performance.
Partner with Brand and Commercial Strategy & Insights on retail media and digital programs at strategic accounts.
Identify and evaluate new e-commerce and direct-to-consumer opportunities.

3. Costco Support & Club Channel

Partner with the VP of Strategic Accounts to support the Costco US and Canada business, including item submissions, programs and business reviews.
Work alongside the Sales & Marketing Admin Assistant on Costco admin, reporting and day-to-day account execution.
Build Club channel knowledge, buyer relationships and program expertise in preparation for taking full ownership of the Club channel.
Long term, own the Club channel, including strategy, annual plans, item and program management, and growth targets.

4. New Business Development

Build and manage the new customer and channel pipeline, with priority targets set in partnership with the SVP of Commercial.
Lead new customer pitches, new item presentations and listing negotiations from first meeting through to first order.
Evaluate new channel opportunities for strategic fit, profitability and supply capacity before committing resources.
Set new business priorities and commercial terms within the approved trade budget.
Track pipeline progress and conversion, and report new customer sales against plan.

5. Account Coverage & Operations

Shape and evolve the coverage model for assigned accounts, building direct customer relationships and internal capability over time.
Own the operating model for retailer portals, promotional planning, deductions and paperwork alongside the Sales Analyst.
Ensure flawless service, promotional execution and retailer compliance across all assigned accounts.

6. Team Leadership

Directly manage the Sales Analyst.
Provide leadership, coaching, development and performance oversight.
Build repeatable account management processes that can scale as the business grows.

7. Cross-Functional Partnership

Partner with Commercial Strategy & Insights on category reviews, selling stories, pricing and promotional ROI.
Provide sales input to the monthly S&OP forecast and work with S&OP and Supply Chain on promotional volumes, new item launches and service levels.
Work with Finance on trade spend, gross-to-net and customer profitability.
Partner with Brand and Product Development on innovation sell-in and launch plans for strategic accounts.
Coordinate with the Sr. Director of Sales and Directors of Sales on shared programs, national initiatives and best practices.

8. Success Measures

Strategic account and e-commerce sales vs. FY27 AOP.
New customer sales vs. plan.
Trade ROI and forecast accuracy (sales input) for assigned accounts.
Account coverage and execution standards met; Club channel transition on schedule.

9. Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Business, Economics or a related field; MBA an asset.
10+ years of CPG sales experience, including direct management of one or more of Walmart US, Kroger, Publix or HEB.
Proven record of winning new customers and listings, and of building joint business plans with national retailers.
Hands-on experience growing an Amazon and e-commerce business, including retail media.
Experience in the Club channel, ideally Costco, and in building direct customer coverage and internal account management capability.
Strong command of trade management, promotional analytics, retailer portals and syndicated data (Circana / NielsenIQ).
Experience leading and developing direct reports.
Ability to travel to customer headquarters and industry events as required.

jobs.title: Sr Director RSM Marketing
jobs.description:
We are committed to connecting Canadians through unique partnerships, our world-class network and content Canadians love—and our innovative team is growing. We are looking for dedicated team members to join our Corporate team who have a genuine passion for making positive impacts on customers and the communities where we live and work. We have a variety of business units with exciting and meaningful work waiting for you, including Communications, HR, Legal and Corporate Affairs, Supply Chain, Finance, and Real Estate. If you are considering your next step, we have exciting opportunities waiting for you. Come build a rewarding career at Rogers and be a driving force behind our success story!

Who We Are Looking For

The Senior Director, Marketing, is the portfolio marketing leader for Rogers Sports & Media, responsible for building audiences, accelerating subscription growth and strengthening the market leadership of our consumer brands. This role sets the integrated brand and go-to-market agenda across the full Sportsnet portfolio, television and specialty brands, streaming products and services, and Rogers’ national radio network of 40+ stations.

Leading a team of 15+ marketers, the Senior Director translates audience insight, content priorities and business goals into distinctive brand platforms, full-funnel marketing plans, partner programs and high-impact advertising. The role works across a complex matrix of content, product, distribution, revenue, media, insights, creative and agency partners to deliver measurable growth and consistent brand experiences across every audience touchpoint.

What You'll Do

Sports The full Sportsnet portfolio, including linear channels, digital platforms, audio, social, direct-to-consumer products and priority league, team and event properties.
Television and specialty Entertainment brands and services across broadcast, specialty, digital and on-demand environments.
Streaming Owned DTC products and partner-distributed OTT offerings across web, apps, connected television and third-party platforms.
Radio Portfolio marketing support for Rogers’ network of 40+ stations, strengthening local relevance while leveraging national scale
Grow audiences across platforms Increase reach, consideration, tune-in, engagement and frequency across linear, digital, audio, social and streaming platforms by connecting priority content with clearly defined audience and fan segments.
Accelerate DTC and OTT subscription growth Build integrated acquisition, onboarding, engagement, retention and win-back programs that grow paid subscriptions, improve customer lifetime value and reduce churn across owned services and third-party partner networks.
Maximize partner-distributed growth Develop scalable joint marketing, merchandising and promotional programs with BDU, connected-TV, device and streaming partners to expand discovery, conversion and usage.
Protect and extend market leadership Maintain strong leadership positions for Rogers Sports & Media brands in every market in which they operate through differentiated positioning, consistent brand stewardship, local relevance and disciplined competitive response.
Improve marketing effectiveness Establish clear portfolio KPIs, measurement frameworks and optimization routines that connect marketing investment to audience, subscriber, revenue and brand outcomes.
Build one high-performing portfolio team Create a clear operating model, shared standards and an inclusive performance culture that strengthens capabilities, develops talent and improves speed, quality and accountability.
Portfolio Strategy and Brand Leadership Set the multi-year portfolio marketing strategy and annual integrated marketing roadmap, aligning audience, subscriber, revenue and brand objectives across Sportsnet, television, streaming and radio.
Define and steward brand promises, positioning, architectures, identities and customer experiences, ensuring each brand is distinctive while contributing to the strength of Rogers Sports & Media and Rogers.
Translate consumer, fan, cultural and market insight into prioritized growth opportunities, audience segments and go-to-market plans.
Guide brand and product alignment across content, platforms and distribution models, ensuring a consistent experience from awareness through consumption and loyalty.
Act as a senior marketing advisor to business and content leaders, bringing a portfolio view to investment choices, market opportunities and competitive challenges.
Audience and Subscriber Growth Lead always-on and tentpole marketing strategies that grow audiences for priority sports, shows, personalities, stations, franchises and platforms.
Own the marketing strategy across the customer lifecycle, including awareness, consideration, acquisition, onboarding, engagement, retention, churn reduction and reactivation.
Partner with product, analytics and revenue teams to improve conversion, engagement, retention and lifetime value across DTC and OTT products.
Develop channel and platform merchandising strategies that improve content discovery and consumption across owned and partner environments.
Build joint business and marketing plans with distribution partners, including BDUs, OTT aggregators, connected-TV platforms, device ecosystems and other strategic partners.
Cultivate league, team, talent, content and commercial partnerships that expand reach, deepen fan engagement and create differentiated audience experiences.
Integrated Marketing, Advertising and Creative Excellence
Lead development of full-funnel marketing plans and advertising calendars across paid, owned, earned, social, experiential, partnership, CRM and on-platform channels.
Set clear strategic briefs and creative standards that inspire distinctive, effective work and support consistent brand delivery across the portfolio.
Oversee campaign development from insight and briefing through media, production, launch, optimization and post-campaign evaluation.
Balance national portfolio priorities with the local market needs of radio stations and regional brands.
Partner closely with internal creative, media agency partners, communications and production teams, as well as external vendors and partners, to deliver work efficiently and at a high standard.
Identify emerging platforms, technologies and marketing approaches that can improve audience experience, marketing effectiveness and speed to market.
Own portfolio marketing budgets and resource planning, directing investment toward the highest-value audience, subscriber and brand opportunities.
Establish annual objectives, benchmarks, scorecards and tactical targets across brand health, audience, subscription, engagement, retention and campaign performance.
Create a disciplined test-and-learn approach, using audience, product and campaign data to optimize investment and improve future planning.
Streamline briefs, governance, approvals and campaign workflows to increase clarity, accountability, speed and operational efficiency.
Build common marketing practices, tools and planning frameworks that can be leveraged across brands, products and business units.
Maintain strong agency, vendor and platform relationships while ensuring appropriate commercial discipline, quality and performance.
Lead, coach and develop a diverse team of 15+ marketing professionals, setting clear priorities, decision rights and performance expectations.
Build succession strength and provide meaningful development opportunities that expand strategic, digital, commercial and leadership capabilities.
Create an environment of collaboration, curiosity, inclusion, accountability and high performance.
Influence across senior and cross-functional teams, aligning content, product, distribution, sales, revenue, insights, media and creative partners around shared outcomes.
Champion customer- and audience-first thinking throughout Rogers Sports & Media.

Measures of Success

Audience growth across priority linear, streaming, digital, audio and social platforms.
Net DTC and partner-distributed subscription growth, supported by stronger acquisition efficiency, engagement and retention.
Improved content discovery, tune-in, usage and frequency across owned and partner platforms.
Sustained or improved market leadership and brand health across sports, television, streaming and radio brands.
Clear contribution of marketing to revenue, customer lifetime value and portfolio growth.
Higher marketing effectiveness through stronger measurement, optimized media investment and more efficient operating practices.
A high-performing, engaged team with strong talent development, succession depth and cross-functional reputation.

Experience And Qualifications

Progressive senior marketing leadership experience (15+ years) in media, entertainment, sports, streaming, subscription, technology or another complex consumer business.
Demonstrated success leading a multi-brand or multi-product portfolio and translating business strategy into integrated marketing action.
Strong understanding of the Canadian media environment, audience behaviour, sports fandom, broadcast marketing and the evolving streaming ecosystem.
Proven experience driving audience growth and subscription outcomes across DTC and partner-distributed channels.
Expertise in brand strategy, portfolio management, audience segmentation, full-funnel marketing, performance media, CRM and lifecycle marketing.
Demonstrated ability to use brand, product, audience and campaign analytics to make investment decisions and optimize performance.
Experience leading sizable teams and developing next-generation marketing talent.
Ability to lead through influence in a matrixed organization and build trusted relationships with senior executives, content leaders, product teams, partners and agencies.
Strong commercial acumen, including budget ownership, vendor management, prioritization and resource allocation.
Exceptional strategic thinking, communication and executive presentation skills, paired with a bias for action and executional excellence.

Leadership Profile

Audience-obsessed Deeply curious about what makes Canadians watch, listen, subscribe, engage and return.
Enterprise-minded Sees connections across brands and platforms and makes choices for the strength of the total portfolio.
Growth-oriented Combines brand-building ambition with performance discipline and commercial accountability.
Creatively ambitious Raises the quality and distinctiveness of the work while remaining focused on measurable outcomes.
Data-led Uses evidence to sharpen strategy, accelerate learning and improve decisions without losing human insight.
Collaborative and influential Brings diverse partners together, creates clarity and moves complex work forward.
People-first Sets a high bar, coaches with intention and creates opportunities for others to grow.

Key Relationships

Internal

Rogers Sports & Media senior leadership; Sportsnet, Television/Streaming and Radio business and content leaders; Brand, Creative, Media, Communications, Product, Technology, Distribution, Revenue, Sales, Insights, Analytics, Finance and People teams.

External

Media agencies; league, team, talent and content partners; BDU and OTT platform partners; production and technology vendors; and strategic commercial partners.

What’s in It for You?

We believe in investing in our people and helping them reach their potential as valuable members of our team. As part of our team, you’ll have access to a wide range of incredible resources, growth opportunities, discounts and perks, including

Competitive salary and annual bonus.
Competitive and flexible health and dental benefits, pension plan, RRSP, TFSA and stock matching programs.
Discounts Enjoy up to 50% off Rogers services and Blue Jays tickets, 25% off TSC items, and a 20% discount on all wireless accessories sold in Rogers stores.
Paid time off for volunteering.
Company matching contributions to charities you support.

jobs.title: Executive Director
jobs.description:
Homelessness, Social equity

Hiring:
Executive Director

Organization:
Homelessness Society of the Bow Valley

Location:
Canmore, Alberta / Hybrid

Description

The Homelessness Society of the Bow Valley (HSBV) is a community-based charity with a mission to foster a Bow Valley community where everyone has access to safe, warm shelter and programs that support their needs.

HSBV provides a low barrier shelter and programs with the goal to build trust and facilitate individuals' access to the local system of care. We are seeking an Executive Director to join our team and help lead the organization’s continued growth and local impact.

Summary

The Executive Director for the Homelessness Society of the Bow Valley is responsible for the successful leadership and overall management of the organization in accordance with the strategic direction, and policies set by the Board of Directors. This position reports to the Board of Directors and will oversee and participate in program operations, public relations, and financial management.

The Executive Director is responsible for ensuring that the organization is operated in compliance with the Government of Canada Charities Directorate, Government of Alberta Societies Act, Municipal Regulatory Bodies, Public Health Department, the Occupational Health and Safety Act, the Employment Standards Act and other mandated legislative requirements. The Executive Director must present the organization in a professional and respectful manner, and model organizational values for all team members.

Responsibilities

Organizational Leadership & Strategy

Clearly articulate and uphold the vision, mission, values, and strategic direction of the organization.
Ensure that the Board’s directives, policies, strategic plan, and organizational vision are effectively operationalized across all levels.
Support the Board in the development and execution of the strategic plan, organizational policies, and long-term planning.
Lead system mapping and identification of wise practices to inform strategic direction and internal improvements.
Support the Board in planning and executing the Annual General Meeting (AGM) and other meetings as required.

Board Relations & Governance

Act as a key liaison between the Board and staff, fostering strong, transparent communication.
Support Board operations and ongoing Board development and engagement.
Provide insight and recommendations to the Board for organizational growth, risk management, and sector trends.
Support convening of Board members and Board onboarding and offboarding processes.

Operations & Compliance

Oversee day-to-day operations, ensuring they align with organizational goals and values.
Maintain an open, collaborative, and mission-focused management approach.
Ensure compliance with all relevant legislation and regulations, including but not limited to Occupational Health and Safety, Canada Revenue Agency’s Charities Directorate, and Alberta Corporate Registry.
Identify and implement technologies and systems to streamline operations and maximize impact.

Financial Management & Administration

Oversee organizational finances and bookkeeping to ensure strong financial health and transparency.
Support the streamlining of financial management systems and processes
Collaborate with bookkeepers, accountants, and auditors to support preparation and completion of annual audits.
Oversee administrative systems, including file organization, digital and physical record storage, and general office management.

People & Culture

Oversee and support the Program Manager, including participation in hiring and staff performance reviews.
Provide leadership in all human resources functions, including recruitment, onboarding, training, and performance management.
Ensure all HR practices reflect a commitment to equal opportunity, accessibility, and inclusion.
Foster a team culture rooted in equity, diversity, inclusion, and psychological safety.
Promote staff wellbeing and encourage ongoing professional development.

Programs & Impact

Collaborate with team members to guide program design, including defining goals, eligibility, referral pathways, and performance metrics.
Conduct and disseminate annual program reports using the established evaluation and measurement framework.
Suggest and implement strategies for program enhancement based on research and community engagement.
Build and maintain meaningful relationships with community partners, shelters, and change makers in the homeless-serving sector.

Fund Development & External Relations

Oversee fundraising strategies and lead donor engagement, cultivation, and stewardship efforts.
Support identifying and securing long-term, stable funding sources.
Support the planning and execution of fundraising and community engagement events.
Develop and maintain strong relationships with key external stakeholders, including funders, government partners, community organizations, and media.
Represent the organization publicly, advocating for its mission, programs, and impact.

Requirements

Over 5 years of experience in the non-profit sector as well as the human services or related field, preferably in leadership and management.
Experience working with a Board of Directors.
A recent police criminal reference check and vulnerable sector search.
Must be able to work flexible hours.
Demonstrated leadership skills with the ability to lead compassionately with empathy, and purpose.
Excellent communication skills and able to connect with a diverse group of people.
Experience in financial and risk planning management.
Knowledge of local resources available in Bow Valley – Asset

INTERPERSONAL QUALITIES

Confident, personable and approachable.
Exercises discretion and judgement in handling sensitive and confidential information.
Collaborative leadership style.
Creative problem solver and comfortable working independently without directions.
Ability to form meaningful relationships with people of all walks of life.

Compensation

Salary: $80,000 to $90,000
This position does not have benefits but will be provided with a wellness fund of $1,000 and a $25 monthly cell phone stipend which will be self-managed by the Executive Director.
Vacation: 4 weeks

EQUAL OPPORTUNITY

HSBV is dedicated to advancing employment equity and building a diverse, inclusive workplace that reflects the communities we serve across the Bow Valley. We encourage applications from all qualified individuals, including those from equity-deserving groups, such as women, Indigenous Peoples, persons with disabilities, visible minorities, and 2SLGBTQIA+ individuals. We evaluate all candidates based on their skills, qualifications, and suitability for the role.

We are committed to providing a recruitment and employment experience that is accessible and low-barrier. If you require accommodations at any stage of the hiring process, please contact Sarah Lonz, Board Chair, at chair@bowvalleyshelter.ca

TO APPLY

If you are someone who loves a challenge, is oriented for strategic thinking, and are passionate about making a local difference this position is for you!

Email your cover letter and resume to info@bowvalleyshelter.ca

Please mention you saw this at GoodWork.ca

Our Purpose

At Deloitte, our Purpose is to make an impact that matters. We exist to inspire and help our people, organizations, communities, and countries to thrive by building a better future. Our work underpins a prosperous society where people can find meaning and opportunity. It builds consumer and business confidence, empowers organizations to find imaginative ways of deploying capital, enables fair, trusted, and functioning social and economic institutions, and allows our friends, families, and communities to enjoy the quality of life that comes with a sustainable future. Have many careers in one Firm.

Enough About Us, Let’s Talk About You

Lead, mentor, and develop a high-performing internal communications team

Be yourself, and more.

Guru Studio is a creative-driven entertainment company and an industry leader in animated storytelling. For over twenty years, our studio has brought to life some of the most recognizable and beloved children’s properties in the world.

We’re always looking for passionate and committed talent, so come join our dynamic and growing team!

We're looking for a talented and experienced Director of IT - come join our team!

Management + Supervision

Knowledgebase

Strong organizational skills with experience building and maintaining structured IT wikis, network diagrams, SOPs, and company-wide IT policies.

Crofters Food Ltd, known in the grocery aisles as Crofters Organic Fruit Spreads, is the leading manufacturer of organic jams, jellies and fruit spreads in North America. Headquartered in picturesque Parry Sound, Ontario, about two hours north of Toronto, we manufacture a vast array of fruit-based spreads sold in stores across Canada, the United States, and select international markets. From the way we source our fruit, to the way we carefully manufacture our products using forward-thinking sustainable processing techniques, to our innovative, health-conscious formulations, every aspect of our operations receives the care and attention they deserve. A small but mighty team, join us as we look to aggressively scale our business on our mission to become one of the leading organic food brands in North America.

Position Summary

The Sr. Director of Strategic Accounts & New Business Development is responsible for growing Crofter’s largest US retail relationships and building the pipeline of new customers and channels that will drive the company’s next stage of growth. This role directly owns Walmart US, Kroger, Publix, HEB, Trader Joe’s and Harris Teeter, leads the e-commerce channel including Amazon, and supports the Costco business in partnership with the VP of Strategic Accounts, with the long-term goal of owning the Club channel.

Key Responsibilities

1. Strategic Account Leadership

Directly own the Walmart US, Kroger, Publix, HEB, Trader Joe’s and Harris Teeter relationships, including annual customer plans, joint business plans, line reviews and annual negotiations.
Build and execute customer plans that deliver sales, distribution and profit targets for each account within the approved trade budget.
Manage trade spend, the promotional calendar and pricing execution for assigned accounts, with a clear focus on trade ROI.
Develop senior-level relationships with buyers, category managers and customer leadership teams.
Use retailer POS, portal and syndicated data to identify growth opportunities and lead fact-based business reviews.

2. E-Commerce

Own the e-commerce channel, including Amazon, with accountability for sales, profitability and channel strategy.
Manage the Amazon relationship, including vendor or seller operations, assortment, pricing, promotions and advertising investment.
Drive digital shelf execution across Amazon and retailer .com sites: content, ratings and reviews, search visibility and in-stock performance.
Partner with Brand and Commercial Strategy & Insights on retail media and digital programs at strategic accounts.
Identify and evaluate new e-commerce and direct-to-consumer opportunities.

3. Costco Support & Club Channel

Partner with the VP of Strategic Accounts to support the Costco US and Canada business, including item submissions, programs and business reviews.
Work alongside the Sales & Marketing Admin Assistant on Costco admin, reporting and day-to-day account execution.
Build Club channel knowledge, buyer relationships and program expertise in preparation for taking full ownership of the Club channel.
Long term, own the Club channel, including strategy, annual plans, item and program management, and growth targets.

4. New Business Development

Build and manage the new customer and channel pipeline, with priority targets set in partnership with the SVP of Commercial.
Lead new customer pitches, new item presentations and listing negotiations from first meeting through to first order.
Evaluate new channel opportunities for strategic fit, profitability and supply capacity before committing resources.
Set new business priorities and commercial terms within the approved trade budget.
Track pipeline progress and conversion, and report new customer sales against plan.

5. Account Coverage & Operations

Shape and evolve the coverage model for assigned accounts, building direct customer relationships and internal capability over time.
Own the operating model for retailer portals, promotional planning, deductions and paperwork alongside the Sales Analyst.
Ensure flawless service, promotional execution and retailer compliance across all assigned accounts.

6. Team Leadership

Directly manage the Sales Analyst.
Provide leadership, coaching, development and performance oversight.
Build repeatable account management processes that can scale as the business grows.

7. Cross-Functional Partnership

Partner with Commercial Strategy & Insights on category reviews, selling stories, pricing and promotional ROI.
Provide sales input to the monthly S&OP forecast and work with S&OP and Supply Chain on promotional volumes, new item launches and service levels.
Work with Finance on trade spend, gross-to-net and customer profitability.
Partner with Brand and Product Development on innovation sell-in and launch plans for strategic accounts.
Coordinate with the Sr. Director of Sales and Directors of Sales on shared programs, national initiatives and best practices.

8. Success Measures

Strategic account and e-commerce sales vs. FY27 AOP.
New customer sales vs. plan.
Trade ROI and forecast accuracy (sales input) for assigned accounts.
Account coverage and execution standards met; Club channel transition on schedule.

9. Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Business, Economics or a related field; MBA an asset.
10+ years of CPG sales experience, including direct management of one or more of Walmart US, Kroger, Publix or HEB.
Proven record of winning new customers and listings, and of building joint business plans with national retailers.
Hands-on experience growing an Amazon and e-commerce business, including retail media.
Experience in the Club channel, ideally Costco, and in building direct customer coverage and internal account management capability.
Strong command of trade management, promotional analytics, retailer portals and syndicated data (Circana / NielsenIQ).
Experience leading and developing direct reports.
Ability to travel to customer headquarters and industry events as required.

new_jobs.title: Sr Director RSM Marketing
new_jobs.description:
We are committed to connecting Canadians through unique partnerships, our world-class network and content Canadians love—and our innovative team is growing. We are looking for dedicated team members to join our Corporate team who have a genuine passion for making positive impacts on customers and the communities where we live and work. We have a variety of business units with exciting and meaningful work waiting for you, including Communications, HR, Legal and Corporate Affairs, Supply Chain, Finance, and Real Estate. If you are considering your next step, we have exciting opportunities waiting for you. Come build a rewarding career at Rogers and be a driving force behind our success story!

Who We Are Looking For

The Senior Director, Marketing, is the portfolio marketing leader for Rogers Sports & Media, responsible for building audiences, accelerating subscription growth and strengthening the market leadership of our consumer brands. This role sets the integrated brand and go-to-market agenda across the full Sportsnet portfolio, television and specialty brands, streaming products and services, and Rogers’ national radio network of 40+ stations.

Leading a team of 15+ marketers, the Senior Director translates audience insight, content priorities and business goals into distinctive brand platforms, full-funnel marketing plans, partner programs and high-impact advertising. The role works across a complex matrix of content, product, distribution, revenue, media, insights, creative and agency partners to deliver measurable growth and consistent brand experiences across every audience touchpoint.

What You'll Do

Sports The full Sportsnet portfolio, including linear channels, digital platforms, audio, social, direct-to-consumer products and priority league, team and event properties.
Television and specialty Entertainment brands and services across broadcast, specialty, digital and on-demand environments.
Streaming Owned DTC products and partner-distributed OTT offerings across web, apps, connected television and third-party platforms.
Radio Portfolio marketing support for Rogers’ network of 40+ stations, strengthening local relevance while leveraging national scale
Grow audiences across platforms Increase reach, consideration, tune-in, engagement and frequency across linear, digital, audio, social and streaming platforms by connecting priority content with clearly defined audience and fan segments.
Accelerate DTC and OTT subscription growth Build integrated acquisition, onboarding, engagement, retention and win-back programs that grow paid subscriptions, improve customer lifetime value and reduce churn across owned services and third-party partner networks.
Maximize partner-distributed growth Develop scalable joint marketing, merchandising and promotional programs with BDU, connected-TV, device and streaming partners to expand discovery, conversion and usage.
Protect and extend market leadership Maintain strong leadership positions for Rogers Sports & Media brands in every market in which they operate through differentiated positioning, consistent brand stewardship, local relevance and disciplined competitive response.
Improve marketing effectiveness Establish clear portfolio KPIs, measurement frameworks and optimization routines that connect marketing investment to audience, subscriber, revenue and brand outcomes.
Build one high-performing portfolio team Create a clear operating model, shared standards and an inclusive performance culture that strengthens capabilities, develops talent and improves speed, quality and accountability.
Portfolio Strategy and Brand Leadership Set the multi-year portfolio marketing strategy and annual integrated marketing roadmap, aligning audience, subscriber, revenue and brand objectives across Sportsnet, television, streaming and radio.
Define and steward brand promises, positioning, architectures, identities and customer experiences, ensuring each brand is distinctive while contributing to the strength of Rogers Sports & Media and Rogers.
Translate consumer, fan, cultural and market insight into prioritized growth opportunities, audience segments and go-to-market plans.
Guide brand and product alignment across content, platforms and distribution models, ensuring a consistent experience from awareness through consumption and loyalty.
Act as a senior marketing advisor to business and content leaders, bringing a portfolio view to investment choices, market opportunities and competitive challenges.
Audience and Subscriber Growth Lead always-on and tentpole marketing strategies that grow audiences for priority sports, shows, personalities, stations, franchises and platforms.
Own the marketing strategy across the customer lifecycle, including awareness, consideration, acquisition, onboarding, engagement, retention, churn reduction and reactivation.
Partner with product, analytics and revenue teams to improve conversion, engagement, retention and lifetime value across DTC and OTT products.
Develop channel and platform merchandising strategies that improve content discovery and consumption across owned and partner environments.
Build joint business and marketing plans with distribution partners, including BDUs, OTT aggregators, connected-TV platforms, device ecosystems and other strategic partners.
Cultivate league, team, talent, content and commercial partnerships that expand reach, deepen fan engagement and create differentiated audience experiences.
Integrated Marketing, Advertising and Creative Excellence
Lead development of full-funnel marketing plans and advertising calendars across paid, owned, earned, social, experiential, partnership, CRM and on-platform channels.
Set clear strategic briefs and creative standards that inspire distinctive, effective work and support consistent brand delivery across the portfolio.
Oversee campaign development from insight and briefing through media, production, launch, optimization and post-campaign evaluation.
Balance national portfolio priorities with the local market needs of radio stations and regional brands.
Partner closely with internal creative, media agency partners, communications and production teams, as well as external vendors and partners, to deliver work efficiently and at a high standard.
Identify emerging platforms, technologies and marketing approaches that can improve audience experience, marketing effectiveness and speed to market.
Own portfolio marketing budgets and resource planning, directing investment toward the highest-value audience, subscriber and brand opportunities.
Establish annual objectives, benchmarks, scorecards and tactical targets across brand health, audience, subscription, engagement, retention and campaign performance.
Create a disciplined test-and-learn approach, using audience, product and campaign data to optimize investment and improve future planning.
Streamline briefs, governance, approvals and campaign workflows to increase clarity, accountability, speed and operational efficiency.
Build common marketing practices, tools and planning frameworks that can be leveraged across brands, products and business units.
Maintain strong agency, vendor and platform relationships while ensuring appropriate commercial discipline, quality and performance.
Lead, coach and develop a diverse team of 15+ marketing professionals, setting clear priorities, decision rights and performance expectations.
Build succession strength and provide meaningful development opportunities that expand strategic, digital, commercial and leadership capabilities.
Create an environment of collaboration, curiosity, inclusion, accountability and high performance.
Influence across senior and cross-functional teams, aligning content, product, distribution, sales, revenue, insights, media and creative partners around shared outcomes.
Champion customer- and audience-first thinking throughout Rogers Sports & Media.

Measures of Success

Audience growth across priority linear, streaming, digital, audio and social platforms.
Net DTC and partner-distributed subscription growth, supported by stronger acquisition efficiency, engagement and retention.
Improved content discovery, tune-in, usage and frequency across owned and partner platforms.
Sustained or improved market leadership and brand health across sports, television, streaming and radio brands.
Clear contribution of marketing to revenue, customer lifetime value and portfolio growth.
Higher marketing effectiveness through stronger measurement, optimized media investment and more efficient operating practices.
A high-performing, engaged team with strong talent development, succession depth and cross-functional reputation.

Experience And Qualifications

Progressive senior marketing leadership experience (15+ years) in media, entertainment, sports, streaming, subscription, technology or another complex consumer business.
Demonstrated success leading a multi-brand or multi-product portfolio and translating business strategy into integrated marketing action.
Strong understanding of the Canadian media environment, audience behaviour, sports fandom, broadcast marketing and the evolving streaming ecosystem.
Proven experience driving audience growth and subscription outcomes across DTC and partner-distributed channels.
Expertise in brand strategy, portfolio management, audience segmentation, full-funnel marketing, performance media, CRM and lifecycle marketing.
Demonstrated ability to use brand, product, audience and campaign analytics to make investment decisions and optimize performance.
Experience leading sizable teams and developing next-generation marketing talent.
Ability to lead through influence in a matrixed organization and build trusted relationships with senior executives, content leaders, product teams, partners and agencies.
Strong commercial acumen, including budget ownership, vendor management, prioritization and resource allocation.
Exceptional strategic thinking, communication and executive presentation skills, paired with a bias for action and executional excellence.

Leadership Profile

Audience-obsessed Deeply curious about what makes Canadians watch, listen, subscribe, engage and return.
Enterprise-minded Sees connections across brands and platforms and makes choices for the strength of the total portfolio.
Growth-oriented Combines brand-building ambition with performance discipline and commercial accountability.
Creatively ambitious Raises the quality and distinctiveness of the work while remaining focused on measurable outcomes.
Data-led Uses evidence to sharpen strategy, accelerate learning and improve decisions without losing human insight.
Collaborative and influential Brings diverse partners together, creates clarity and moves complex work forward.
People-first Sets a high bar, coaches with intention and creates opportunities for others to grow.

Key Relationships

Internal

Rogers Sports & Media senior leadership; Sportsnet, Television/Streaming and Radio business and content leaders; Brand, Creative, Media, Communications, Product, Technology, Distribution, Revenue, Sales, Insights, Analytics, Finance and People teams.

External

Media agencies; league, team, talent and content partners; BDU and OTT platform partners; production and technology vendors; and strategic commercial partners.

What’s in It for You?

We believe in investing in our people and helping them reach their potential as valuable members of our team. As part of our team, you’ll have access to a wide range of incredible resources, growth opportunities, discounts and perks, including

Competitive salary and annual bonus.
Competitive and flexible health and dental benefits, pension plan, RRSP, TFSA and stock matching programs.
Discounts Enjoy up to 50% off Rogers services and Blue Jays tickets, 25% off TSC items, and a 20% discount on all wireless accessories sold in Rogers stores.
Paid time off for volunteering.
Company matching contributions to charities you support.
